package_info.why_malicious: The injected code on LCBO's checkout page was designed to steal customers’ payment information, constituting a clear case of web skimming/magecart-style attack. This is a direct violation of user trust and payment security, with the explicit goal of exfiltrating sensitive financial data.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user visits checkout page and enters payment info)
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript on LCBO checkout page (likely in HTML or linked JS file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects payment information from the checkout page DOM, then sends this data via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in payment data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive payment data from the user and transmits it to an external, unauthorized server, which is a hallmark of web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout page scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors, not to unknown external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processing scripts may collect and transmit data, but only to authorized, vetted endpoints.
key_indicators: Collection of payment data from DOM
Network request to untrusted external domain
Execution only on sensitive checkout/payment pages

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript into the LCBO checkout page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code when users visit the checkout page.

attack_chain.action: Injected code collects payment information as users enter it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is captured in the browser.

attack_chain.action: Collected payment data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment information (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code collecting payment or personal data from checkout forms
Network requests from checkout pages to untrusted or unknown domains
Unexpected script modifications or injections on payment pages
file_indicators: Injected or modified JavaScript on checkout.html or payment.js
References to external scripts not present in legitimate source control
network_indicators: POST requests from checkout page to domains not associated with payment processors
Unusual outbound traffic from payment page endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized JavaScript changes on checkout/payment pages, inspect network traffic for POST requests to unknown domains during checkout, and alert on any script collecting and transmitting payment data to non-whitelisted endpoints.
